bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \( 1.558 \times 10^{2} \) J for part (ii), the energy per kilogram. That is smaller than the correct value by a factor of exactly \( 10^{3} \), and it is refuted by the key's OWN part (i): a kilomole of oxygen is 32 kg, so part (ii) must be part (i) divided by 32, namely \( 4.986 \times 10^{6} / 32 = 1.558 \times 10^{5} \) J \( \text{kg}^{-1} \). The printed numeral 155.8 is the energy per GRAM (\( 4986 / 32 \)), so the exponent belongs to joule per gram, not joule per kilogram. A sanity check settles it independently: a single mole of oxygen, only 32 g, already carries 4986 J at this temperature, so one kilogram cannot carry 156 J. The correct answer is \( 1.558 \times 10^{5} \) J \( \text{kg}^{-1} \); parts (i) and (iii) of the printed key are correct.]
